issues.problem: "Each lit cell tugs the needle through its dial" says each photocell has its own dial wired straight to the needle. The film's own bible says the Mark I reached the response unit 'through a randomly wired association layer', and the weights (claim mk1-weights) sat on those connections, not on the 400 cells. The picture is already more faithful than the line: at 34.29 s the lit cells' threads pass through the patch tangle and fan out to several dials (about 80 on the board, not 400). The 'an illustration of the rule' caption covers the simplified board, but this narrated sentence is about 'it', the Mark I.
issues.fix: Re-narrate as "Each lit cell tugs the needle through the dials it is wired to, and the total decides." (or "...through the dials it feeds..."). Re-anchor the 'dial' and 'decides' beats in ch01-s03 to the new word timings. The visual needs no change.

issues.problem: "Behind it ran a nest of wires" is supported only by the bible ('patch board of tangled cables'), not by research/claims.json, which the brief makes the only allowed source. Racks, dials and motors are covered by mk1-weights; the wiring is not.
issues.fix: No text change. Research adds and verifies a claim, e.g. 'mk1-patchboard: the Mark I's photocells were connected to its association units through a patch board, with the connections wired at random' (Wikipedia 'Perceptron'; Smithsonian NMAH object 334414). Then cite it on ch01-s02 in script.json.

fairnessNotes: Even-handed. The limit is stated as a property of the machine ('it could learn only simple patterns'), not as a verdict on neural networks. The contested story that Minsky and Papert 'killed' the field is left out entirely instead of being told one-sidedly. No lab or company is named or favoured in the lineage line. Rosenblatt is shown upright in era-plain shirtsleeves, not as a likeness, with an accurate role card ('Frank Rosenblatt · psychologist'). No quotes are used, as the brief requires.
